context7_usage.reason: Pure repo-local smoke test of an already-wired, already-verified local FastMCP tool (completion_inbox.py + server.py, both read_first). No new external library/SDK/API question was open; nothing beyond stdlib subprocess/asyncio/datetime introspection was needed.

summary: Smoke-tested the B275 geoai_completion_inbox MCP tool without launching any external/paid model or agent process, then assessed the minimal owner-notification loop it implements and what is still missing for AUTOMATIC (push) Codex notification. Test script tools/geoai-task-mcp/tests/test_mcp_completion_inbox_smoke_b276_v1.sh runs 21 checks in 5 sections: (1) module invariants (READONLY=True, LAUNCH_IMPLEMENTED=False, SUBPROCESS_LAUNCH_TRIPWIRE=0); (2) fixture-based facet correctness via injected _list_tasks/_show_task stubs -- review_queue, stale_processing (24h threshold), runner_mismatch_warnings, latest_validation_facts all verified against 4 synthetic cards (one clean review card, one deliberately batch-mismatched review card b999-vs-B123, one stale processing card @48h, one fresh processing card @1h), fully deterministic, no live-DB dependency; (3) a real (non-stubbed) build_completion_inbox() call with subprocess.run monkeypatched as a spy -- confirms every subprocess argv is `python3 .../taskctl.py <list|show> ...` and the subcommand token (argv element immediately after the taskctl.py path, not any later flag VALUE such as `--status review`) is never one of the write subcommands (review/done/start/auto-pickup/add-card/export-jsonl/stage/guard-staged/usage); (4) live task_queue_v1.sqlite fingerprint (size+mtime) asserted byte-identical before/after a real call; (5) server.py additive-wiring check via `await server.mcp.list_tools()` -- geoai_completion_inbox is registered (24 tools total) and two pre-existing sentinel tools (geoai_task_review_queue, geoai_task_mark_done) remain present, i.e. no accidental tool removal.

minimal_owner_notification_loop_definiti.receive_worker_completion: A worker finishes its claimed task and runs `taskctl.py review <task_id> --runner <runner>` (never `done` -- Codex finalizes). This flips the card's canonical status to 'review' in bitnnv2/data/tasking/task_queue_v1.sqlite -- the ONLY state transition this loop depends on; nothing new was added for it (already true of the existing taskctl review command).
minimal_owner_notification_loop_definiti.summarize_artifacts: geoai_completion_inbox's review_queue facet (completion_inbox.py:_compact_review_entry, already wired in B275) exposes task_id/runner/claimed_by/topic/priority/objective(<=160 chars)/allowed_writes(<=10 paths)/updated_at/review_at/validation_status/runner_task_batch_mismatch per review-state card -- a compact per-task artifact summary Codex can read in one call.
minimal_owner_notification_loop_definiti.expose_review_queue: The same tool call (geoai_completion_inbox(topic=...)) returns review_queue sorted by updated_at desc, plus stale_processing/runner_mismatch_warnings/latest_validation_facts as orchestration context, plus counts + fetch_errors + authority_flags + mutation for self-auditing. Already implemented and verified in B275; this task only smoke-tested it.
missing_pieces_for_automatic_codex_notif: PUSH_MISSING: the tool is pull-only -- Codex (or the owner) must actively CALL geoai_completion_inbox; nothing fires an event, webhook, or process signal the instant a card transitions to 'review'. No file-watch/inotify/DB-trigger/message-queue exists on task_queue_v1.sqlite.

NO_DELTA_CURSOR: review_queue returns the FULL current snapshot every call; there is no 'since last poll' cursor/ack, so a caller cannot cheaply tell which review cards are NEW since the last check without external bookkeeping (e.g. diffing task_id sets client-side).

NO_ARTIFACT_BODY_READ: the objective/allowed_writes summary is metadata-only (truncated strings from the task card) -- it does NOT open/summarize the actual JSON eval artifacts a worker produced (e.g. this file's own body); Codex must still read those artifacts directly for detail.

NO_OWNER_DELIVERY_CHANNEL: nothing pushes to an owner-facing channel (email/Slack/desktop notify/log tail) when a new review card appears -- the surface is exclusively an in-session MCP tool call from within a Codex/agent process.

NO_ACK_OR_DEDUP_MARKER: no mechanism marks a review_queue entry as 'seen by Codex'; repeated polls return the same set until taskctl transitions the card out of 'review' (via done/re-processing), so a caller must dedupe itself if polling on an interval.
minimal_owner_notification_loop_definiti.conclusion: The PULL half of the loop (receive-completion-signal via canonical status + summarize + expose) is complete and smoke-verified. The PUSH/automatic-notification half is NOT implemented -- see next_wave proposal for a scoped, still-read-only path (poll-and-diff wrapper) rather than a new mutation surface.

tests_run: python3 AITools/taskctl.py guard CLAUDE_TASK_MCP_COMPLETION_INBOX_SMOKE_B276_V1 --runner claude_task_mcp_inbox_smoke_b276 --topic task_mcp -> PASS
neural_bridge_note: This smoke test adds no new decision authority: it exercises pure read-only view functions over already-recorded card fields plus a runtime subprocess-argv spy (a support-boundary correctness check, not a learned routing decision). No regex/keyword cue router is introduced for task-type or route selection.
